claim: No morphological or syntactic annotation of the Samaveda Samhita (Kauthuma Arcika or any sakha) is published in any public resource reachable from here.
verified_by: agent 9, Wave 2, by independent enumeration rather than by inheriting Wave 0's conclusion
why_this_is_a_proof_and_not_a_deferral: Each of the three resources was enumerated in full and the enumeration is reproducible from the recorded method. The negative is therefore a measured absence over a stated search space, not an unfinished pipeline. It is the BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE case.

independent_negatives.resource: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit, CoNLL-U release
independent_negatives.enumeration_method: GitHub git trees API on the dcs subtree sha 21766ccd413c79dac0d4b42a115786e0a4b23a9a with recursive=1; truncated=false; 23,576 entries. The contents API was NOT used because it caps at 1,000 entries and the Atharvavedic directory alone holds 1,038 blobs.
independent_negatives.note: Samavedic ritual literature is well served; the Samhita itself is absent.

independent_negatives.enumeration_method: every '# citation_text=' value in the three CoNLL-U files, counted
the public /api/texts and /api/resources indexes, read in full on 2026-09-15

what_would_change_this: A published morphological or syntactic annotation of the Samaveda Samhita. None was found. The standing rule against model-guessed Vedic analysis applies with particular force here, because Arcika verses are largely Rigvedic borrowings, which makes a wrong answer both especially plausible and especially hard to detect.
what_was_done_instead: 216 of 1,844 Arcika verses whose letter skeleton is IDENTICAL to a Rigvedic verse carrying an analysis were given that analysis, typed CROSS_VEDA_TEXT_IDENTITY. 1,628 abstained, each with a reason on its row. This is not a Samavedic annotation and is not presented as one.
